stories.title: P0: fix scripts/pair_obdlink.sh (Trixie bluez prompt regex + display-capable agent) so a durable bond + trust is written
stories.completionNotes:
BENCH HALF DONE, all 4 AC met. ENGINE-ON acceptance is Spool's and is NOT discharged here.

I CAPTURED THE REAL BYTES BEFORE WRITING THE MATCHER, and that is the whole story of this story. Atlas's note described both bugs accurately and I would STILL have shipped a half-fix from the description alone. Recorded a live bluetoothctl session off the Pi (bluez 5.82, adapter 88:A2:9E:84:46:1D): the prompt is `\x1b[0;94m[bluetoothctl]> \x1b[0m`. The obvious fix -- swap `#` for `>` -- leaves a SECOND trap armed, because THE ANSI ESCAPE ITSELF CONTAINS A `[`, so the old greedy `\[.+\]#` spans from the escape into the prompt even on a `#` box. One regex, two independent defects, and only the raw bytes show the second. PROMPT_PATTERN now forbids `[`/`]` inside the bracket body and accepts either terminator, so legacy `[bluetooth]#` boxes keep working (US-475's DoD asked for that).

FREE FINDING FROM THE SAME CAPTURE, load-bearing for BL-025: `devices Paired` returned EMPTY -- there is NO bond of any kind on this Pi, on any device. That turns BL-025's bond-less diagnosis from inference into a measurement. Radio reads Powered: yes, so US-514's rfkill fix is holding. Recorded in specs/architecture.md 3.4.

THE REAL DELIVERABLE WAS NEITHER BUG -- IT WAS THE HEREDOC. The driver lived in `python3 - <<'PYEOF'`. Heredoc code cannot be imported, therefore cannot be tested, therefore two defects sat for months in a file that LOOKED maintained (proper header, stated invariants, shellcheck-clean wrapper). Moved to scripts/pair_obdlink_driver.py with the session logic pexpect-FREE behind a thin PexpectChild adapter (pexpect is Pi-only, absent on this Windows box -- otherwise the whole suite would skip). 33 driver tests + 5 wiring pins, all RED first.

THE HARNESS FOUND A BUG NOBODY KNEW ABOUT, and it is the argument for verbatim fixtures: bluetoothctl REDRAWS ITS PROMPT SEVERAL TIMES AT STARTUP, so `sendline(cmd); expect(PROMPT)` matches a STALE prompt and `before` returns terminal PADDING as if it were the command's reply -- a SILENT WRONG ANSWER (every `info` read would have parsed as 'no bond'), strictly worse than the hang I was sent to fix. Fixed by anchoring on each command's own pty echo first. A hand-written 'prompt goes here' fixture passes this happily.

THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS, PM/ATLAS MAY OVERRULE. (1) SUCCESS NOW MEANS A DURABLE BOND: 'Pairing successful' is bluez's word for the LINK, so the driver re-reads `info` after `trust` and FAILS unless Paired+Bonded+Trusted -- the old script printed '--- pair + trust successful ---' having checked nothing, which was a claim, not a reading, and reboot-survival is the actual AC. (2) IDEMPOTENT WITHOUT --force: an existing durable bond is reported and LEFT ALONE, because re-pairing needs the dongle powered (engine on) and a reflexive `remove` on a working bond strands the car; a PARTIAL bond IS cleared first, since that half-state is what makes `pair` fail AlreadyExists. (3) scan on -> wait -> scan OFF -> pair (Atlas's live-proven ordering; an active discovery competes with the handshake on one radio).

AC-4 PRESERVED AND PROVEN: --dry-run still short-circuits before any preflight, and the existing sentinel-shim test (a fake bluetoothctl on PATH that writes a file if called) still passes. Ran the real --dry-run and read its 7 preview lines.

TEST-HYGIENE TRAP WORTH COPYING: my regression pins grepped for `NoInputNoOutput` and `PYEOF` and BOTH FAILED -- on the header comments that DOCUMENT the defect. A pin that greps a defect's NAME fires on its own documentation. Strip comments + the module docstring (ast gives tree.body[0].lineno/end_lineno) and then TEST THE STRIPPER, because a stripper returning nothing makes every pin pass vacuously.

US-475 IS THIS SAME DEFECT, shelved 2026-07-20 as an 'architect hallucination'. Its own shelve note says revisit ONLY IF a real re-pair failure is observed on the Pi -- Atlas ran it live 07-31 and got the TIMEOUT, so the shelve trigger fired on its own terms. Its DoD is a strict subset of what shipped. RECOMMEND RETIRE-AS-DELIVERED so it is not built twice.

GREEN (synchronous, in-loop): tests/pi/obdii = 674 passed / 1 skipped (shellcheck absent), exit 0. ruff clean on all 3 touched .py; bash -n clean. HOST GAPS unchanged (Sprints 64/65/66): make, black, mypy absent on this Windows box -- PM PLEASE RUN MYPY AT INTEGRATION, the driver is a new typed module. NO deploy change needed: sync_tree rsyncs scripts/ wholesale (verified against deploy-pi.sh's exclude list), so the driver lands beside the script.

FILED TD-070: docs/bluetooth-setup.md's ~20 manual transcript blocks still show the legacy `[bluetooth]#` prompt + a non-display agent. Added a BANNER now so it stops actively misleading the operator; the full refresh is cheap to fold into the engine-on session while a real transcript is on screen.

ENGINE-ON GATE OWED (Spool/CIO, cannot be discharged from this box): dongle powered + solid blue LED -> `bash scripts/pair_obdlink.sh 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB` -> '--- pair + trust successful ---'; `bluetoothctl info` Paired/Bonded/Trusted all yes; then REBOOT and re-check, because reboot survival IS the acceptance and a green run is not. WATCH FOR: if it now reaches `pair` and fails THERE, that is PROGRESS not regression -- the old failure was a TIMEOUT before any command ran, so a bluez error at the pair step proves the transport fix worked and isolates the remaining fault to the SSP handshake / pair-mode.
acceptance: fix the pexpect prompt regex: it expects `\[.+\]#` but Trixie bluetoothctl prompts `[bluetoothctl]>` -> it times out and never pairs. Match the real prompt

change the agent from `NoInputNoOutput` (contradicts the script's own Confirm-passkey handling -> auth-fails on the OBDLink) to a display-capable agent (`DisplayYesNo`) so a durable bond + `trust` is written and survives reboot
